rv.q: Dogstar deserves credit for its originality, in how it walks a tonal tightrope few could pull off.

Recent RADA graduate Abdul Jalloh is excellent as Sam, a young whaler who can be a bit annoying as he insists on sticking to the rules. But now he's on his first trip and it's all going terribly wrong. Jalloh captures earnest Sam's desperate desire to please the captain and be promoted to the role of harpooner.
DOGSTAR is a quirky oddity with a few flaws but surprising charm.

So Dogstar journeyed farther and farther north in search of its elusive prey. Now it has been stuck in Arctic ice for months. We join the ship shortly before the first mate succumbs to a painful death.

cn.t: Hall's dark comedy about 19th-century whalers trapped in ice draws mixed reviews, with critics finding the isolated setting and sardonic humor more uneven than her debut, though performances register.
